sections.h2: Which Darke County offices handle your property tax?
sections.html:
In Darke County the auditor decides what a parcel is worth, and the treasurer turns that value into a bill and takes the money. Both offices are in the Darke County Courthouse at 504 S. Broadway in Greenville, and both open weekdays from eight in the morning until four in the afternoon.

The auditor also publishes the county real estate website. It offers a parcel search, a map, a sales report, a delinquency report, a tax estimator and a conveyance fee calculator, and it hosts the downloadable forms mentioned below.

sections.h2: What does the Darke County housing picture look like?
sections.html:
Darke is a farm county on the Indiana border, with Greenville as its seat and only city. The 2020 count put 71.7 percent of residents in rural areas, and the county runs roughly 600 square miles.

That census listed 22,599 housing units, with 7.4 percent empty, and about three of every four occupied homes were lived in by their owners. Owner-heavy farm country means many sellers hold acreage, outbuildings or a house on a split-off lot, and each of those touches a separate tax rule.

  • School districts in the county include Greenville City, Versailles Exempted Village, Ansonia Local and Arcanum-Butler Local.
  • The southeast edge touches Montgomery County, so some owners commute toward Dayton.
  • Manufacturing supplies 26.6 percent of jobs in a state profile cited by the county's Wikipedia entry.

sections.h2: How often does the Darke County auditor revalue homes?
sections.html:
The county's page for the auditor describes a general reappraisal of all real property every six years, with an update three years after each one. Between cycles a value moves only for new building, demolition, a lot split or a Board of Revision order.

The auditor's forms page lists the tax-year valuation duplicates, including the one that is collected in 2027, along with tax rates for each year from 2009 on. Rates differ by taxing district, so one house value gives a different bill inside Greenville than in a village school district. Try the tax estimator, then ask the real estate division which district your parcel belongs to.

sections.h2: What dates does the state set for paying Darke County tax?
sections.html:
ORC 323.12 gives owners two routes: one payment covering the year by December 31, or a first half by that day and a second by June 20. A check that arrives late still counts if the envelope bears a Postal Service postmark from the last day or earlier. A mark from a private postage meter does not help.

Read the dates on your own bill, because the treasurer may keep the books open a little longer for a collection period. The real estate site has a tax payment cart for paying online.

  • A lender that escrows your tax should hear that you hold a copy of the bill.
  • Owing back tax? Check the delinquency report on the auditor's site, then call the treasurer for a payoff number before the house is listed.

sections.h2: What is the process for disputing a Darke County value?
sections.html:
A disputed value starts with state form DTE 1, which goes to the auditor and then to the Board of Revision. ORC 5715.19 sets March 31 of the following tax year as the limit, extended to the close of first-half collection when that date is later.

The auditor's forms page carries the DTE 1, the board's rules of practice, and a second form, DTE 2, for complaints about something other than market value. The statute adds a few rules that affect sellers.

  • State the dollar amount by which you say the value is wrong.
  • Taxes on the claimed value may be tendered while the matter is pending; a final value above that figure brings interest on the gap.
  • Refiling in the same reappraisal period needs a change since the last complaint: an arm's-length sale, casualty loss or a major improvement.
  • A ruling is due within 180 days after the filing deadline, and the hearing notice goes out at least ten days ahead.
  • Give the board every piece of evidence you hold, since withheld evidence can be barred on appeal.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can Darke County owners use?
sections.html:
Three programs come up most often: the homestead credit, the owner-occupied residence reduction, and farmland valuation at its current agricultural use. Each one has its own application on the auditor's forms page.

The auditor's homestead question page sets three routes in: turning 65 by December 31 of the filing year, being permanently and totally disabled on January 1, or being a surviving spouse who was at least 59 when the spouse died. The applicant also has to own the home and occupy it as a main residence on January 1. The page shows a $40,000 income ceiling for 2024 applicants, indexed each September, and describes the credit as the tax on $28,000 of true value. Call the auditor for the figures that apply this year. The forms are DTE 105A for the application and DTE 105E for a disability certificate. A prior-year application filed late is accepted through December 31.

For farmland, application DTE 109 requests current agricultural use value. ORC 5713.30 requires at least ten acres in commercial agricultural use during the three years before filing, or fewer than ten acres that averaged $2,500 or more in gross yearly income. When a sale ends that status, a recoupment charge covering the tax savings can follow.

sections.h2: Do repairs or additions before a Darke County sale need permits?
sections.html:
They can. The county building regulation office at 520 S. Broadway, reached at 937-547-7379, requires permits and inspections for residential and commercial electrical work, heating and cooling work, and construction, which the county's page defines as all new building, additions and replacements. Its reach covers the unincorporated areas, the city of Greenville and a list of villages: Ansonia, Arcanum, Castine, Gettysburg, Ithaca, New Madison, New Weston, Pitsburg, Union City, Versailles, Wayne Lakes and Yorkshire.

For a building permit the office asks for drawings that show a foundation plan, a floor plan, bearing wall cross sections, roof detail and exterior elevations. Construction also needs sign-off from the Darke County Health Department at 937-548-4196. Zoning is a separate layer: cities, villages and townships hold that authority, and owners in an unzoned area contact a township trustee. The zoning inspector at 937-547-7381 takes questions about a township's zoning and about splitting off a lot.

Ask the building office which permits cover your repairs before you list, and keep the approved paperwork with your sale file.

sections.h2: What local features affect a Darke County home sale?
sections.html:
Road and travel patterns decide a lot of listings here. The county highway garage, working under the county engineer, maintains 521 miles of county roadway and 530 bridges, and state routes such as US 127 and US 36 cross the county. The Darke County Airport sits on State Route 121 near Versailles.

Events shape short-term demand around a few towns. Eldora Speedway near New Weston hosts large dirt-track races, Versailles holds the Poultry Days festival that has drawn crowds as large as 50,000, and Greenville hosts a festival honoring its sharpshooting native. A branch of Edison State Community College is in Greenville.

sections.h2: What happens with the tax when a Darke County house sells?
sections.html:
Before the deed reaches the recorder, the buyer files a conveyance fee statement with the auditor on form DTE 100, or DTE 100EX when an exemption applies. The seller pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax at that point, and the auditor stamps the deed.

The statement also asks about homestead and farmland. Where the property carried a homestead or owner-occupancy reduction, the two sides sign a sworn instrument that deals with how that reduction ends, and farmland that was under agricultural valuation gets its own statement on form DTE 102. The auditor's conveyance fee calculator adds the parcel transfer fee to the total.

If any tax is delinquent, get a payoff figure from the treasurer so the title company can fold it into the closing numbers.

faqs.q: Which office issues a Darke County tax bill?
faqs.a: The treasurer, at 937-547-7365. The auditor's real estate division, at 937-547-7308, answers questions about the value behind the bill.

faqs.q: What is the last day to contest a Darke County value?
faqs.a: March 31 of the following tax year, unless first-half collection closes later. The DTE 1 goes to the auditor.

faqs.q: Does Darke County have a tax credit for older owners?
faqs.a: Yes. The Ohio homestead program covers owners aged 65 or older, disabled owners and qualifying surviving spouses. Apply on DTE 105A and ask the auditor which income limit applies.

faqs.q: Is a sale possible with tax still owed in Darke County?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a payoff figure from the treasurer, and use the auditor's delinquency report to see what is posted against the parcel.

faqs.q: How do I find the rate for my Darke County parcel?
faqs.a: Try the tax estimator on the real estate website or the yearly rate pages in the auditor's forms list, and confirm your taxing district by phone.
